edit.description: `harness_diagnostics(&harness_path, &layers)?` (:240) aborts BEFORE the reporter match (:242-249), so a harness that fails to LOAD never reaches any reporter: miette renders the error to stderr and main exits non-zero with an empty stdout. For `--reporter session-start` that is the placement silently passing — Claude Code's SessionStart hook reads stdout JSON, so the session opens with no temper context and no verdict at all. Catch the load error, lower it to one `error` Diagnostic, and run the SELECTED reporter over it. Terminal/GitHub/SARIF keep exiting non-zero; session-start keeps its advisory exit 0 (the comment at :255 already states why) but MUST print its payload.

The lowering helper's home — `Diagnostic` is defined here (:47). A `miette::Report` (the load failure) becomes one `error` Diagnostic whose rule id names the failure class and whose message carries the report's own text plus temper's own consequence: the gate did not run this session, so nothing in the harness was checked. Do NOT assert a Claude Code hook-loading consequence in the message without a retrieved cite at the site (collaboration rule, external facts).

`session_start` (:118 builds the failing-verdict header and NOTIFY_INSTRUCTION into `additionalContext`, capped at :39's 10k limit) must render the load-failure diagnostic the same way it renders a contract failure — one diagnostic source, every placement (distribution.md, same section). Verify the cap logic still holds when the single diagnostic is a long miette message.

Regression: a harness whose `.claude/settings.json` is not parseable JSON — `json_manifest::Manifest::parse` raises `JsonManifestError::Malformed` (json_manifest.rs:267) through `compose.rs:1324`'s `?` — still prints a well-formed SessionStart payload on stdout, exit 0, whose `additionalContext` names the offending file and states the gate did not run. Pin non-vacuity: the payload is not the clean-pass shape (0048's conservation bar).
The terminal reporter over the same broken harness still renders the failure and still exits non-zero — the fix must not soften the hard placements while it un-silences the advisory one.

The one out-of-fence assertion the fix inverts. `a_lock_carrying_two_requirement_rows_with_the_same_name_refuses_loud` (:534) asserts `findings.is_empty()` with the comment "a fatal duplicate key error produces no findings (the check exits before collecting them)" — it PINS the bug this entry removes. Keep `assert!(!success, ...)`; replace the empty-findings assertion with exactly one `gate.load-fault` finding naming the colliding key `docs` (`common::findings_for(&findings, "gate.load-fault")`), and update the comment: the fatal error is no longer discarded, it is the run's single diagnostic, which is what lets the advisory placement speak it. The test's subject — refuse loud, never silently shadow one requirement with the other — is unchanged.

summary: A harness that fails to load aborts before any reporter runs, so the session-start placement contributes no verdict at all — it silently passes.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: an unparseable .claude/settings.json still yields a SessionStart JSON payload on stdout naming the file and stating the gate did not run, never an empty stdout
the terminal reporter over the same harness still exits non-zero with the failure rendered
a duplicate-identity-key lock still exits non-zero AND now yields exactly one `gate.load-fault` finding naming the colliding key, instead of an empty finding set

acceptance: `temper check . --reporter session-start` on a harness whose source cannot be loaded prints a well-formed SessionStart payload carrying the failure, rather than exiting with an empty stdout — the section's 'never silently passes' held for load errors, not only contract failures. The hard placements (terminal, GitHub, SARIF) still exit non-zero, and the duplicate-key load fault now reports one `gate.load-fault` finding rather than none. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
notes: Fence widened 09-07 from .flume/refactor/build-session-start-load-error-out-of-fence-test.md: the fix was worked out green on every suite but tests/gate_fail_loud.rs, which pins the pre-fix contract. Does NOT cover the hooks manifest — a session whose settings.json will not parse never invokes the SessionStart hook, so no reporter can reach it; that half is GUARD-UNPARSEABLE-MANIFEST-WRITE-REFUSAL. scoped at 1aae63b5

edit.description: New well-formedness check beside nested_member_admissibility (~60-79, the real neighbor — not satisfies_label_admissibility, which judges a different, host-blind ambiguity): a single host declaring the SAME (kind, key) nested member twice is a malformed lock, refused at admissibility. Two DIFFERENT hosts sharing a (kind, key) are NOT coincident under 0049's grammar (`spec:alpha/invariant/x` and `spec:beta/invariant/x` are distinct addresses) — that case is a resolution-time ambiguity, not an admissibility refusal; see graph.rs below.

`member_named` (:1650) is the ONE membership lookup `resolves` (:1632), `edge_resolves` and `member_at` all read since ab500f80 consolidated them, and its own doc comment already names this entry's ruling as owed: a bare key `also names an embedded member, taking whichever member of the kind carries it first ... which of several same-keyed members it means is an open ambiguity, and refusing it is a policy decision owned elsewhere`. Decide it here. Because ab500f80 also made an embedded member's identity ITS ADDRESS (`compose::embedded_member_features`), the host is now read straight off `features.id` via `parse_nested_address` — no plumbing, no carrier to thread. When a BARE (unqualified) key matches more than one nested member of a kind across different hosts, refuse at resolution (a new graph.route finding) naming every colliding host; the full host-qualified address always resolves unambiguously. `by_kind`'s pooled per-kind Vec (compose::embedded_features_by_kind, :1139) is what pools the candidates a bare key sees.
explain's bare-name resolution needs the same ambiguity refusal as graph.route, naming every host a bare/explain name could mean — why_impl (~538) currently collapses same-kind matches to the first.

embedded_hosts_by_source (:572) is the last partial implementation of "which host owns this nested member": it builds a `(kind, key) -> host` BTreeMap off nested_member rows with a plain `.insert()` (:578), so a cross-host duplicate silently keeps whichever row inserts last, feeding mention_reachable's citation scoping. It also hand-parses the host address a fourth time (`row.host.split_once(':')`, :577) where `graph::parse_nested_address` owns that grammar. Read the host off the member's own address — ab500f80 put it there — and give this the same ambiguity judgment, rather than a third lookup with a third failure mode (engineering.md, "One job, one home").

Three regressions: (1) one host declaring the same (kind, key) nested member twice refuses at admissibility; (2) two different hosts each declaring a same-kind-same-key nested member: a bare/explain-name reference to that key refuses at resolution naming both hosts, while either host's full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` address always resolves; (3) the same cross-host duplicate reaching embedded_hosts_by_source (a body-carried edge citation scoped through it) is judged the same way, not silently mapped to whichever host inserted last.

The one out-of-fence test that pins the prior policy this entry overturns: `embedded_edge_targets::a_bare_nested_member_address_matches_first_same_key` (:1188, in tests/graph.rs) builds two `service` hosts each declaring a `domain` member keyed `common`, spells the bare `common` on an edge, and asserts `run.ok` because "bare nested member addresses should resolve to the first match (ambiguous but deterministic)". That IS the codified ambiguity `graph::member_named`'s doc calls "a policy decision owned elsewhere", so deciding it necessarily rewrites this test — into the refusal naming both carrier hosts, or into a host-qualified spelling that still resolves. Same corpus, inverted verdict; keep the case.

summary: A duplicate (kind, key) nested member is coincident only within one host; across hosts a bare address is ambiguous at resolution, never silently picked.

tests.asserts: same-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses at admissibility; cross-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses only a bare/unqualified reference, at resolution, naming both hosts, across every bare-key consumer (graph::resolves, explain's why_impl, embedded_hosts_by_source) — and tests/graph.rs's bare-key edge case is re-pinned to the same verdict
a bare nested-member address matching two hosts refuses at resolution naming both, where the suite previously asserted first-match-wins; the host-qualified spelling of either still resolves

acceptance: A host repeating its own (kind, key) nested member refuses loud at admissibility. Two different hosts sharing a (kind, key) are legal (distinct addresses per 0049); a bare or explain-name reference ambiguous between them refuses at resolution naming every host, while the full host-qualified address to either always resolves. The refusal matches the SDK's, which SHIPPED this same bar at c60ddd3f (sdk/src/emit.ts:337-347: names every carrier host and points at the whole `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` spelling) — one verdict at both ends of the seam, not two wordings. The bar fires at every consumer of a bare key, not only graph::member_named: explain's why_impl and embedded_hosts_by_source (gate.rs) each name every candidate host too. The regression pins non-vacuity: each case asserts at least one real colliding pair is judged, not an empty read short-circuiting to 'no ambiguity' (0048's conservation bar).
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (GH #51 half); corrected at bf4b4168. Plumbing shipped with EMBEDDED-MEMBER-HOST-CARRIED-NOT-SMUGGLED (ab500f80): identity IS the address, three lookups are one `member_named`, only the judgment is left. Fence widened 09-07 from .flume/refactor/build-nested-member-bare-key-refusal-needs-tests-graph.md — the implementation was built green except one out-of-fence test pinning the old policy. scoped at 1aae63b5

edit.description: `committed_layout_sites` (:54) collects discovered committed members of LAYOUT-content kinds only, so 676467cf's undeclared-member finding never sees a composed kind. Generalize it to one site walk over every discovered non-`local` kind, tagging each site with its content class, and keep the layout branch's rule id and message byte-identical so tests/layout_kind.rs stays green untouched. Gate the whole check on lock presence: on an unrepresented harness (no `.temper/lock.toml`, the default-contract auto-adoption path) every discovered member is undeclared and the finding must stay silent. Thread the undeclared set into the `coverage_note::check` call (:544) so the disclosure can count it apart.

Beside `undeclared_layout_members_from_doc` (:2820): the composed-kind counterpart. A composed member's whole trace on the lock is its projection provenance row, not the five `MEMBER_ADDRESS_COLUMNS` declaration families a layout host reaches through — so this one joins each discovered site's `source_path` against `read_prior_provenance_from_doc` (:2272), the same rows `emit_owned_targets` (:3268) and `config_stale` (:2713) already walk. A discovered document at a represented kind's locus that no provenance row names is reported `locus.undeclared-member` at `warn`, naming path and kind: `emit` will never maintain it (orphan classification walks lock rows, so it reports 0 orphan-drift over it) and `guard` never bound it, yet Claude Code loads it. Remedy named first is declare the member and re-emit; the `local` remedy is spellable for a custom kind only — a built-in cannot be re-declared until BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS lands — so the message must not offer it as if it always were.

`check` (:57) renders `coverage.checked` (:28) from `member_counts` alone, so a stranger document at a governed locus inflates a kind's count with no mark — the observed 11 -> 13. Take the undeclared set gate.rs now computes and disclose declared and undeclared apart per kind, so the one line that says what was checked cannot silently absorb a member the program does not declare. Hard constraint: the line stays BYTE-IDENTICAL when a kind has zero undeclared members — `tests/snapshots/gauntlet__check_diagnostics.snap:7` pins the whole rendering and `tests/gate_fail_loud.rs:228` asserts the `skill (1)` substring, so the undeclared mark appends only where there is one.

The fixtures here already build harness dirs with a committed lock and read findings back off the GitHub reporter's one-line-per-finding form (`write_skill`, `lock_widget_kind`, `check_harness`), which is exactly this entry's shape. Four regressions, per tests[].

The gauntlet corpus's whole `coverage.checked` rendering is pinned here (:7). Its members are all declared, so the disclosure change must leave this snapshot unmoved — it is in the fence so a genuine, justified move can be accepted rather than reverting the tick on the fence, not as licence to reformat the line.

summary: A document dropped at a represented kind's locus that the lock declares no member for is admitted, counted, and never named — the file-locus half of 676467cf.

tests.asserts: an undeclared `.claude/rules/*.md` in a represented harness yields one `locus.undeclared-member` warn naming its path and kind, and the `coverage.checked` disclosure counts it apart from the declared members of that kind

the same harness with that document declared and emitted reports neither the finding nor an undeclared count — and asserts a non-zero declared count first, so the silence is not an empty read (0048's conservation bar)
an unrepresented harness (no lock) checked under the built-in default contract reports no `locus.undeclared-member` at all, however many documents discovery finds

acceptance: Invariant 6's "no read or lowering represents less than it was given" holds for a discovered document with no declared member: `check` names it, the disclosure counts it apart, and neither fires on an unrepresented harness or on a declared-and-emitted one. 676467cf's `layout.undeclared-member` keeps its rule id and wording — tests/layout_kind.rs is untouched and green. The `coverage.checked` rendering is unchanged wherever no kind has an undeclared member — `tests/snapshots/gauntlet__check_diagnostics.snap` does not move. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
notes: Routed from inbox 09-07 (cascade-integrations, GH #58, observed at ab61fea4). Re-verified this tick at 1aae63b5: gate.rs:66 filters sites to `Content::Layout`, and drift.rs:1414's orphan classification walks lock rows only, so a disk file with no row is invisible to `emit`. Worse in direction than the layout case — the stranger is silently present in what Claude Code loads. Guard half is GUARD-UNDECLARED-LOCUS-WRITE. scoped at 1aae63b5

edit.description: `guard` (:832) allows outright any path not equal to a lock-declared emit-owned target (:843-846) — so creating `.claude/rules/stray.md` in a REPRESENTED harness passes, while the no-lock fallback (:850, `is_claude_path`) would have bound the very same write. Representation currently loosens the boundary. Bind a write whose path falls inside a represented committed kind's `governs` locus but matches no emit-owned target: the program declares no member there, `emit` will never maintain the file, and Claude Code loads it anyway. Judged through the existing `GuardVerdict`/enforcement-mode path, never escalated past the declared mode; the message names the kind whose locus it landed in and the declare-and-re-emit remedy CHECK-UNDECLARED-MEMBER-AT-A-GOVERNED-LOCUS's finding names. Locus matching goes through `globset` (the one glob engine, already inside `ignore`), never a hand-rolled suffix test. A `local`-commitment locus is never bound — its documents are the author's own by declaration.

`Command::Guard` (:332) already reads `declarations` (:346) and `emit_owned_targets` (:349) before the stdin read; hand `install::guard` the represented committed kinds' loci off the same `declarations` (each `KindFactRow`'s `governs_root`/`governs_glob`, skipping `commitment == local` and any kind with no file locus). No new disk read and no walk — the guard runs on every tool call, so the cost bound is the existing one.

Regressions beside the existing guard cases, per tests[]. Pin the unchanged arms explicitly: a write to a declared projection keeps its current verdict verbatim, and the no-lock `.claude/` fallback is untouched.

summary: In a represented harness the guard allows any write outside the lock's exact projection paths — including creating an undeclared document inside a governed locus.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: block mode denies (exit 2) a Write creating an undeclared `.claude/rules/*.md` in a represented harness, naming the `rule` kind whose locus it landed in; warn surfaces in-band and allows; note allows silently
a write to a lock-declared projection keeps its existing verdict, a write to a `local`-commitment locus is never bound, and an unrepresented harness keeps the `.claude/` fallback unchanged

acceptance: The guard's binding no longer depends on a path being an exact lock row: a write into a represented committed kind's locus that declares no member there is judged at the author's declared enforcement mode, so a represented harness is at least as protected as an unrepresented one. Every existing guard arm — declared projection, represented manifest, local locus, no-lock fallback — reports the same verdict it does today. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
notes: Routed from inbox 09-07 (cascade-integrations, GH #58, observed at ab61fea4), the guard half of CHECK-UNDECLARED-MEMBER-AT-A-GOVERNED-LOCUS. Verified at 1aae63b5: install.rs:844 returns Allow for any non-target path once a lock exists. Cascade's position — a partly represented harness opts a locus down explicitly, never by silence — is the acceptance here; the opt-down is `local`, spellable for a custom kind and awaiting BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS for a built-in. scoped at 1aae63b5

edit.description: Audit every admissibility diagnostic's message text — e.g. clause_collision_diagnostics (~167, message ~184-189 names only the shared label) — so each names the concrete edit (which two clauses/members collided and the argument that discriminates them) rather than restating lock/contract state alone.
Audit diagnostic construction call sites for the same bar where messages are assembled rather than authored at the diagnostic definition.

tests.asserts: admissibility refusal messages name the discriminating edit, not just the lock state

edit.description: read_collection_member (222) takes a LayoutMember's leaves from its immediate sub-headings only, keyed by slug; the paragraph directly under the member's own heading lands nowhere. Land it under whichever reserved leaf key `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules — composed leaves are author-named (NestedMemberRow.leaves keyed by field name, no reserved own-span key exists there; the SDK's `FRAMEWORK_KEYS`/kind.ts:245 `prose` is a member-level value, not a leaf-name reservation). Hazards the fork must rule on: node.body includes sub-heading text (the own span must cut at the first child heading), and a sub-heading slugged to the reserved name would collide with it.
Regression: a layout collection member whose body is `### Title` + a paragraph + `**Test.** ...` (no sub-headings) materializes a non-empty leaves map carrying the paragraph under the ruled key.

FRAMEWORK_KEYS (~245) reserves `prose` as a member-level value only; once `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules a reserved own-span leaf key, an author's sub-heading slugging to that same name needs a collision guard (or explicit precedence rule) — the exact key and whether it joins FRAMEWORK_KEYS stays whatever the fork rules, not invented here.

summary: A layout collection member's own paragraph span lands nowhere — not a leaf, not the lock, not explain — while its sub-headings' spans do.

tests.asserts: a layout collection member's own span (the text directly under its heading) lands in its leaves, under the ruled reserved key

acceptance: A layout collection member's own paragraph (not just its sub-headings) reaches a leaf, addressable and visible to leaf predicates, leaf addresses, and explain, matching the composed half's full-leaves behavior. Per 0048's conservation bar, the regression pins non-vacuity: it asserts the captured own-span text is non-empty before checking it resolves as a leaf.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (F11, GH #43 leaves gap); corrected at bf4b4168: 'the composed half already names it prose' is false — no reserved own-span leaf name exists anywhere in the corpus today. Reserving one is a Decision, tracked by fork `layout-own-span-leaf`; this entry waits on it. Re-chained at e6c551cc behind KINDS-IN-PLAY-NAME-COLLISION-REFUSAL: its old parent shipped, leaving tests/layout_kind.rs + sdk/src/kind.ts contended with three live entries. scoped at e6c551cc

edit.description: Add `relocate(base, delta)` beside the existing `kind()` factory (~431 — shifted from ~336 by f8ba355b's discriminated-union narrowing, verified on disk 09-07). KindFacts is now three inlined object-literal union branches, one per locus shape (~168-310), each already near-fully duplicated by design (that commit's own rationale: no intermediate named types requiring root-level exports). A spread-merge (`{...base, edgeFields: delta.edgeFields}`) should stay within whichever branch `base` already is and type-check as KindFacts without touching all three by hand — confirm this holds under real tsc rather than assuming, since a marker field no branch currently declares (e.g. `facts.relocates`) is exactly the case a discriminated union complicates; if it doesn't type-check cleanly, a side-channel marker (outside KindFacts) is the fallback, not a third duplication of the union. Mark the produced facts with a relocation marker (e.g. `facts.relocates`) so KINDS-IN-PLAY-NAME-COLLISION-REFUSAL can later tell a legitimate relocation from a genuine name collision.
SDK-side payload assertion: a relocated `rule` kind declaring an added edgeField emits the fact in its compiled declarations (no `as any`, no dropped field).

Rust regression: the emitted edge fact from a relocated built-in resolves a real graph.route edge — proving no engine change is needed, since edges are always read from assembly `edge` rows keyed by `from` kind (never carried on a kind row itself); `graph.route` isn't assertable from an SDK test, hence the split.

This file already carries the corpus's one existing relocation vocabulary — a lock-row `row_relocates_builtin` (src/compose.rs:1091) recognizes a same-named row as a legitimate built-in relocation purely structurally (format/unit_shape/registration compatible), with no marker field at all, and doesn't examine edgeFields either — so a corpus kind named `rule` with an added edgeField should already flow through that existing Rust-side path with no engine change (matching this entry's own claim). Before minting a new `facts.relocates` marker in the SDK, confirm it doesn't duplicate `row_relocates_builtin`'s concept under a second name; if the marker is genuinely SDK-layer-only (needed before compilation to a KindFactRow), name that distinction explicitly rather than leaving two same-purpose 'relocates' vocabularies unreconciled. Extend this file's relocated-built-in fixtures if a new end-to-end case is the cleanest proof.

`row_relocates_builtin` is DEFINED here (:1091) and read at :460/:1114 — the corpus's one existing 'relocates' vocabulary. Where the entry concludes the SDK-side `facts.relocates` marker is a distinct, SDK-layer-only concept, that distinction is named at this definition's doc comment so the two vocabularies are reconciled in the same diff, not left as two same-purpose names. Behaviour unchanged: overlay_builtin_kind (:453) never carries edgeFields. Read-only mentions at src/kind.rs:94, src/admissibility.rs:123/426 and tests/lock_declaration_rows.rs:1878 are prose that rides the next entry opening those files (standing prose-cite rule), not this fence.

summary: A built-in kind cannot take an added edge field; the SDK has no sanctioned relocation constructor and an as any cast drops the edge fact silently.

tests.asserts: a relocated built-in kind's added edge field is emitted, not silently dropped by an as any cast

acceptance: A corpus can add an edge field to a built-in kind (e.g. rule) via the sanctioned relocation form and have it resolve a real graph edge, checked at check and rendered at emit — no as any cast needed. No engine change required: overlay_builtin_kind (compose.rs:453) never needs to carry edgeFields, since edges never live on a kind row. Per 0048's conservation bar, the regression pins non-vacuity: it asserts the relocated kind's edge fact is actually present (non-empty) in the compiled declarations before checking it resolves a real edge.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (GH #54); reworded at bf4b4168, item g. f8ba355b moved the kind() factory to kind.ts:431 and made KindFacts a 3-branch locus union; files[] carries that caveat. Ripple reconciled 09-07: src/compose.rs added — row_relocates_builtin's definition is where the two 'relocates' vocabularies get reconciled. scoped at ab61fea4

edit.description: `narrate_kind` (:530) renders three strands — guidance and cite, layout regions plus skeleton, hosted kinds — and nothing else, so on a kind with no member yet it prints one guidance line and stops. Two more strands the `KindFactRow` it already holds can render today: (i) the **locus** — `collection_address` (which manifest and key path a registration member keys at) plus the `registration` channel labels for a registration kind, and `governs_root`/`governs_glob` for a file-locus kind, so `explain kind:hook` finally says where a hook member lands; (ii) the **address form** — how a reference to a member of this kind is spelled, read from the single address-grammar home MEMBER-ADDRESS-GRAMMAR-ONE-HOME establishes (`src/member_address.rs`, that entry's new file), never a fourth hand-spelling. Both must render with zero members of the kind in the corpus — the adopter's actual moment, and the reason this is not `corpus_leaves` (:817), which can only report what existing members carry.

Regressions on a MEMBER-LESS surface, per tests[] — the non-vacuity bar is that the fixture carries zero members of the explained kind, so the lines cannot be coming from a corpus read. Keep the existing arm where a kind declaring none of the strands still prints its clean "nothing declared" line rather than falling silent.

summary: `explain kind:<x>` never says where a member of the kind lands or how a reference to one is spelled — the two lines an adopter with no member yet most needs.

tests.asserts: `explain kind:hook` on a surface with zero hook members names its `hooks.<Event>` collection address and the address form a reference to one of its members takes

`explain kind:rule` on a surface with zero rule members names its file locus and its `kind:name` address form; a kind declaring no locus, layout, guidance or hosted kind still prints the "nothing declared" line

acceptance: On a surface carrying no member of the kind, `explain kind:<name>` prints where a member of it lands and how a reference to one is spelled, alongside the guidance, layout and hosted-kind strands 3dcc73f1 already renders — the read verb narrating a kind, not only a kind that already has members. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
notes: Routed from inbox 09-07 (cascade's assessment of EXPLAIN-KIND-ADOPTER-ENTRY-POINT, observed at ab61fea4; re-verified at 1aae63b5). Their third line — the leaves an embedded kind's members will carry, before any member exists — is NOT here: a kind declares no field set anywhere (sdk/src/kind.ts has no leaf schema, and `corpus_leaves` reads members), so it is the open fork `(kind-declared-leaf-schema)`. Blocked on the grammar consolidation so the address form has one writer. scoped at 1aae63b5

edit.description: kindsInPlay's `admit` closure (~351-355) is first-wins by name — `if (byName.has(facts.name)) return;` — walking harness.members in authored order, so a corpus kind reusing a built-in's name at a different root is silently discarded before it ever reaches the engine's own kind.admissibility check (admissibility.rs:126, joined_kind_admissibility:484 — which already refuses a diverging same-name row, but only once one reaches the lock). Change `admit` to compare the two KindFacts values and refuse a divergence, naming both loci — except when the second carries BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS's relocation marker (`facts.relocates`), which this must recognize and allow.

Regression via the harness's compile path (compileDeclarations): a harness declaring a corpus kind under a built-in's exact name at a different root refuses at load, naming both loci; the sanctioned relocation form still passes.

The Rust-side twin of this refusal already exists and is tested here: compose::partition_kind_rows/row_relocates_builtin judges a same-named lock row as a legitimate relocation or a collision purely structurally, with no marker field. If BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS's `admit` comparison in kindsInPlay ends up replicating that same format/unit_shape/registration compatibility test in TS (rather than inventing a `facts.relocates` flag), an end-to-end fixture here proves the two layers agree; note which design landed.

summary: A corpus kind reusing a built-in's name at a different root is silently discarded by kindsInPlay's first-wins-by-name, with no diagnostic anywhere.

tests.asserts: two distinct KindFacts values sharing one name refuse at load unless one is the sanctioned relocation of the other

acceptance: Declaring a corpus kind that reuses a built-in's name at a different root refuses loud, naming both loci, unless authored through the sanctioned relocation form.
